question_text: What does the abbreviation "14 CFR" stand for?

options.text: Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations.

explanation_correct: 14 CFR stands for Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations — the title containing all federal aviation regulations including Part 107.

explanation_distractors.B: There is no '14th Circuit Federal Register.' CFR stands for Code of Federal Regulations.
explanation_distractors.C: CFR does not stand for Civil Flight Rules. It is the Code of Federal Regulations.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: In FAA publications, what does "AC" stand for?
explanation_correct: AC stands for Advisory Circular — FAA informational documents that provide guidance and best practices on aviation topics.

explanation_distractors.B: Air Carrier is not abbreviated AC in FAA terminology. AC refers to Advisory Circular.
explanation_distractors.C: Aircraft Certificate is not the meaning of AC. Advisory Circulars are FAA guidance documents.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "ACS" stand for in the context of FAA pilot testing?
explanation_correct: ACS stands for Airman Certification Standards — the document that defines the knowledge, risk management, and skills required for FAA pilot certificates and ratings.

explanation_distractors.B: Aircraft Control System is not what ACS stands for in the testing context.
explanation_distractors.C: ACS does not refer to a communication service. It defines certification testing standards.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ADDS stands for Aviation Digital Data Services — a web-based weather resource for pilots that includes METARs, TAFs, PIREPs, and other aviation weather products.

explanation_distractors.B: ADDS is not related to drone detection. It is a weather data service.
explanation_distractors.C: ADDS is not a departure data sheet. It provides digital weather products for aviation.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ADIZ stands for Air Defense Identification Zone — airspace over land or water where the identification, location, and control of aircraft is required in the interest of national security.

explanation_distractors.B: ADIZ has nothing to do with instrument departures. It is a national security airspace zone.
explanation_distractors.C: ADIZ predates drone regulations. It is an Air Defense Identification Zone.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ADM stands for Aeronautical Decision-Making — a systematic process for identifying hazards, assessing risk, and choosing safe courses of action.

explanation_distractors.B: ADM does not refer to departure management. It is a decision-making framework.
explanation_distractors.C: ADM is not about data monitoring. It is a structured approach to aviation risk management.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: AFM stands for Airplane Flight Manual — the FAA-approved document containing operating limitations, procedures, and performance data for a specific aircraft.

explanation_distractors.B: AFM does not refer to frequency management. It is the official flight manual for an aircraft.
explanation_distractors.C: In aviation context, AFM means Airplane Flight Manual, not Air Force Manual.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "AFS" stand for in FAA organizational structure?
explanation_correct: AFS stands for Flight Standards Service — the FAA office responsible for certification and oversight of airmen, air operators, and air agencies.

explanation_distractors.B: AFS is not an airport survey. It refers to the FAA's Flight Standards Service.
explanation_distractors.C: AFS is not a fire service. It is the Flight Standards Service within the FAA.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: AGL stands for Above Ground Level — height measured from the surface directly below the aircraft. Part 107's 400 ft altitude limit is measured in AGL.

explanation_distractors.B: AGL does not refer to guidance limits. It is a measurement of height above the ground.
explanation_distractors.C: AGL has nothing to do with latitude. It means Above Ground Level.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: AIRMET stands for Airman's Meteorological Information — advisories for significant weather conditions at intensities lower than those requiring a SIGMET, including IFR conditions, mountain obscuration, turbulence, strong surface winds, and icing.

explanation_distractors.B: AIRMET is not an airport terminal. It is a weather advisory product.
explanation_distractors.C: AIRMET has nothing to do with instrument ratings. It is a weather advisory.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "AOA" stand for in aerodynamics?
explanation_correct: AOA stands for Angle of Attack — the angle between the wing's chord line and the relative wind. Exceeding the critical AOA causes a stall.

explanation_distractors.B: Area of Approach is not what AOA stands for. It describes the angle of the wing relative to airflow.
explanation_distractors.C: AOA is not an altitude measurement. It is a fundamental aerodynamic concept.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ATC stands for Air Traffic Control — the service operated by the FAA to promote the safe and efficient flow of air traffic. Part 107 requires ATC authorization for controlled airspace operations.

explanation_distractors.B: ATC does not refer to a certificate. It is the Air Traffic Control service.
explanation_distractors.C: ATC is not a training center. It is the Air Traffic Control system.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ATD stands for Aviation Training Device — a training tool that replicates aircraft instruments and controls for ground-based practice.

explanation_distractors.B: ATD is not a transport document. It is a device used for pilot training.
explanation_distractors.C: ATD does not refer to an airport district. It is an Aviation Training Device.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: In weather reports, what does "CB" stand for?
explanation_correct: CB stands for Cumulonimbus — towering thunderstorm clouds associated with severe turbulence, icing, hail, lightning, and wind shear. These are hazardous to all aircraft.

explanation_distractors.B: Cloud Base is not abbreviated CB. CB specifically means Cumulonimbus thunderstorm clouds.
explanation_distractors.C: CB has nothing to do with boundaries. It identifies dangerous thunderstorm clouds.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: CFA stands for Controlled Firing Areas — airspace where activities such as weapons testing are conducted under conditions that ensure the safety of non-participating aircraft. CFAs are not charted because activities are suspended when aircraft are detected.

explanation_distractors.B: CFA is not related to frequency assignments. It designates areas with controlled weapons firing.
explanation_distractors.C: CFA does not refer to flight authorization. It is a type of special use airspace.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: CFR stands for Code of Federal Regulations — the codification of the general and permanent rules published in the Federal Register by U.S. executive departments and agencies.

explanation_distractors.B: CFR does not stand for Certified Flight Requirements. It is the Code of Federal Regulations.
explanation_distractors.C: CFR is not a flight record. It is the complete collection of federal regulations.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "CG" stand for in aircraft operations?
explanation_correct: CG stands for Center of Gravity — the balance point of the aircraft system. An improper CG can degrade stability and control.

explanation_distractors.B: Control Group is not what CG means in aviation. CG refers to the balance point of the aircraft.
explanation_distractors.C: CG is not navigation guidance. It is the Center of Gravity.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "CP" stand for in aerodynamics?
explanation_correct: CP stands for Center of Pressure — the point along the wing chord where the total aerodynamic force is considered to act. Its position changes with angle of attack.

explanation_distractors.B: Critical Point is not the aviation meaning of CP. CP describes where aerodynamic forces concentrate.
explanation_distractors.C: Constant Power is not what CP means. It refers to the Center of Pressure on an airfoil.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: CRM stands for Crew Resource Management — the effective use of all available resources (people, equipment, information) to improve safety and decision making during flight operations.

explanation_distractors.B: CRM is not about crash recovery. It focuses on proactive safety through resource management.
explanation_distractors.C: CRM has nothing to do with route mapping. It is a team-based safety management approach.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: CTAF stands for Common Traffic Advisory Frequency — used for airport advisory practices at non-towered airports. The CTAF may be a UNICOM, MULTICOM, FSS, or tower frequency.

explanation_distractors.B: CTAF is not a controlled tower frequency. It is the Common Traffic Advisory Frequency.
explanation_distractors.C: CTAF does not refer to a terminal area. It is used for traffic advisories at non-towered airports.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: CTP stands for Certification Training Program — an FAA-required training program for certain pilot certificates.

explanation_distractors.B: CTP is not a pilot certificate. It is a training program requirement.
explanation_distractors.C: CTP has nothing to do with traffic patterns. It is a Certification Training Program.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: DPE stands for Designated Pilot Examiner — an individual authorized by the FAA to conduct practical tests for pilot certificates and ratings.

explanation_distractors.B: DPE is not about drone evaluation. A DPE conducts pilot checkrides on behalf of the FAA.
explanation_distractors.C: DPE has nothing to do with departure procedures. It is a Designated Pilot Examiner.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: DVFR stands for Defense VFR — a VFR flight plan that must be filed for flights operating within an Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ).

explanation_distractors.B: DVFR is not a flight route. It is a Defense VFR flight plan required in an ADIZ.
explanation_distractors.C: DVFR does not mean Designated VFR. The D stands for Defense.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: EMS stands for Emergency Services — medical and rescue services. Drone pilots must avoid interfering with EMS operations.

explanation_distractors.B: EMS is not an electronic system. It refers to Emergency Services such as medical helicopters and first responders.
explanation_distractors.C: EMS does not refer to maintenance. It stands for Emergency Services.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: FAA stands for Federal Aviation Administration — the U.S. government agency responsible for regulating civil aviation.

explanation_distractors.B: The FAA is not called the Federal Airspace Authority. It is the Federal Aviation Administration.
explanation_distractors.C: FAA does not stand for Flight Authorization Agency.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: FADEC stands for Full Authority Digital Engine Control — a system that manages all aspects of engine performance digitally.

explanation_distractors.B: FADEC is not a defense command. It is an engine management computer system.
explanation_distractors.C: FADEC is not a console. It is a Full Authority Digital Engine Control system.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: In the context of the alcohol and drug testing rules, what does "FDA" stand for?
explanation_correct: FDA stands for Federal Drug Administration — the agency relevant to medication and substance regulations that affect pilot fitness for duty.

explanation_distractors.B: FDA does not refer to duty assignments. It is the Federal Drug Administration.
explanation_distractors.C: FDA has nothing to do with drone authorization.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "FDC" stand for in the context of NOTAMs?
explanation_correct: FDC stands for Flight Data Center — a regulatory NOTAM type. Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs) are issued as FDC NOTAMs.

explanation_distractors.B: FDC is not a drone command. FDC NOTAMs are regulatory notices from the Flight Data Center.
explanation_distractors.C: FDC does not mean Flight Dispatch Control. It is the source of regulatory NOTAMs.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: FL stands for Flight Level — a standard nominal altitude expressed in hundreds of feet (e.g., FL180 = 18,000 feet MSL). Flight levels begin at 18,000 feet MSL.

explanation_distractors.B: FL does not mean Final Leg. It designates altitude levels above 18,000 feet.
explanation_distractors.C: FL is not related to fuel. It is a pressure altitude reference.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: FRZ stands for Flight Restriction Zone — a defined area of airspace (most notably around Washington, D.C.) where flight is restricted or prohibited.

explanation_distractors.B: FRZ does not refer to radar. It is a Flight Restriction Zone.
explanation_distractors.C: FRZ has nothing to do with fuel. It restricts flight in certain airspace.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "FS" stand for in FAA services?
explanation_correct: FS stands for Flight Service — providing pilot briefings, weather, NOTAM processing, flight plan services, and aeronautical information.

explanation_distractors.B: FS does not mean Federal Security. It is Flight Service.
explanation_distractors.C: FS is not related to fuel. It refers to the Flight Service system.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: FSDO stands for Flight Standards District Office — local FAA offices responsible for certification and surveillance of airmen, flight schools, and air operators.

explanation_distractors.B: FSDO is not about drones specifically. It is a general FAA field office.
explanation_distractors.C: FSDO is not a dispatch office. It oversees flight standards in a geographic district.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: IAP stands for Instrument Approach Procedures — series of predetermined maneuvers for the orderly transfer of an aircraft under instrument flight conditions.

explanation_distractors.B: While 'Initial Approach Point' is a concept, IAP officially stands for Instrument Approach Procedures.
explanation_distractors.C: IAP is not an international protocol. It refers to instrument landing procedures.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ICAO stands for International Civil Aviation Organization — the United Nations agency that sets international aviation standards and practices.

explanation_distractors.B: ICAO is not about commercial airlines. It is the UN agency for international civil aviation standards.
explanation_distractors.C: ICAO is an international body, not an interstate oversight agency.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: IFR stands for Instrument Flight Rules — the rules governing flight when visual reference to the ground is not possible. Part 107 operations are conducted under VFR, not IFR.

explanation_distractors.B: IFR is not about restrictions. It is a set of flight rules for low-visibility conditions.
explanation_distractors.C: IFR is not international. It is the Instrument Flight Rules system.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: On sectional charts, what does "IR" stand for?
explanation_correct: IR stands for Instrument Routes — military training routes flown under IFR. On sectional charts, IR routes with four-digit numbers are flown at or below 1,500 ft AGL.

explanation_distractors.B: IR does not mean Inactive Runway. It labels Instrument Routes for military training.
explanation_distractors.C: IR is not an instrument restriction. It identifies specific military training routes.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: ISA stands for International Standard Atmosphere — a model atmosphere used as a reference (15°C at sea level, standard pressure 29.92 inHg). Deviations from ISA affect density altitude.

explanation_distractors.B: ISA is not a safety advisory. It is the standard model atmosphere used in aviation calculations.
explanation_distractors.C: ISA has nothing to do with security. It is the International Standard Atmosphere.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: LAA stands for Local Airport Advisory — a service provided by facilities at airports not served by a control tower, giving pilots information about wind, runway, and traffic.

explanation_distractors.B: LAA is not a type of approach. It is a local advisory service.
explanation_distractors.C: LAA does not refer to authorization. It is a Local Airport Advisory service.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "MAP" stand for in instrument procedures?
explanation_correct: MAP stands for Missed Approach Point — the point in an instrument approach at which the pilot must execute a missed approach if the runway is not in sight.

explanation_distractors.B: MAP does not refer to a maximum altitude. It is the decision point on an instrument approach.
explanation_distractors.C: MAP is not a military pattern. It is the Missed Approach Point.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: MDA stands for Minimum Descent Altitude — the lowest altitude to which descent is authorized on a non-precision instrument approach until the pilot sees the required visual references.

explanation_distractors.B: MDA is not related to drones. It is a non-precision instrument approach altitude.
explanation_distractors.C: MDA does not mean Military Defense Area. It is the Minimum Descent Altitude.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: MEL stands for Minimum Equipment List — a document that allows an aircraft to be operated with certain items of equipment inoperative under specific conditions.

explanation_distractors.B: MEL is not an elevation reference. It lists equipment that may be inoperative for dispatch.
explanation_distractors.C: MEL has nothing to do with military equipment. It is a Minimum Equipment List.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: MFD stands for Multi-functional Displays — cockpit screens that can show multiple types of information including navigation, weather, and traffic.

explanation_distractors.B: MFD is not a distance measurement. It refers to electronic display screens.
explanation_distractors.C: MFD has nothing to do with military directives. It is a cockpit display system.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: MOA stands for Military Operations Area — airspace established outside Class A to separate certain nonhazardous military activities from IFR traffic and identify the area for VFR pilots.

explanation_distractors.B: MOA is not an altitude requirement. It is a type of special use airspace.
explanation_distractors.C: MOA does not mean Maximum Operating Area. It designates military training airspace.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: MSL stands for Mean Sea Level — many charted altitudes, airspace floors, and ceilings are expressed as feet above MSL.

explanation_distractors.B: MSL is not a safety limit. It is the reference datum for altitude measurement.
explanation_distractors.C: MSL has nothing to do with lateral separation. It means Mean Sea Level.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: MTR stands for Military Training Route — routes used for military training at airspeeds greater than 250 knots. Routes with 4-digit numbers are flown at or below 1,500 ft AGL.

explanation_distractors.B: MTR is not a transition rate. It identifies routes for high-speed military training flights.
explanation_distractors.C: MTR has nothing to do with terrain restrictions. It designates Military Training Routes.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: NACG stands for National Aeronautical Charting Group — the organization responsible for producing aeronautical charts including sectional and terminal area charts.

explanation_distractors.B: NACG is not a control grid. It produces the charts pilots use for navigation.
explanation_distractors.C: NACG has nothing to do with approach control. It is the charting organization.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Pilots may file confidential safety reports through NASA's ASRS (Aviation Safety Reporting System).

explanation_distractors.B: NASA is not a safety authority. It is the space and aeronautics research agency.
explanation_distractors.C: NASA is not a surveillance agency. It conducts aeronautics and space research.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: NAS stands for National Airspace System — the common network of U.S. airspace including air navigation facilities, equipment, services, airports, and rules.

explanation_distractors.B: NAS does not mean non-authorized space. It encompasses all U.S. airspace and supporting infrastructure.
explanation_distractors.C: NAS is not a geographic sector. It is the National Airspace System.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "NM" stand for in aviation?
explanation_correct: NM stands for Nautical Miles — used for aviation distances and speed references (knots). One nautical mile equals approximately 1.15 statute miles.

explanation_distractors.B: NM does not refer to an operating mode. It is a unit of distance.
explanation_distractors.C: NM is not a navigation marker. It stands for Nautical Miles.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: NOAA stands for National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration — the agency that provides weather data including aviation weather products.

explanation_distractors.B: NOAA is not an aviation authority. It focuses on oceanic and atmospheric science.
explanation_distractors.C: NOAA is not an observation agency. It is the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "NOTAM" stand for according to current FAA terminology (2025)?

options.text: National Operations and Traffic Advisory Message.

explanation_correct: NOTAM stands for Notice to Airmen. FAA Order JO 7930.2U changed the term back to 'Notice to Airmen' effective 2025.

explanation_distractors.B: 'Notice to Air Missions' was briefly used but the current FAA order reverted to Notice to Airmen.
explanation_distractors.C: NOTAM does not stand for any version with 'Traffic Advisory Message.'

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "NSA" stand for in aviation charting?
explanation_correct: NSA stands for National Security Area — airspace where there is a requirement for increased security of ground facilities. Flight in NSAs is voluntarily avoided.

explanation_distractors.B: NSA is not labeled a 'no-fly' area. Pilots are requested but not required to avoid them.
explanation_distractors.C: NSA does not mean non-standard airspace. It is a National Security Area.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "OTC" stand for in the context of pilot medications?
explanation_correct: OTC stands for Over-the-Counter — referring to medications available without a prescription. Some OTC medications can impair pilot performance.

explanation_distractors.B: OTC in the medication context is not a certificate. It describes non-prescription drugs.
explanation_distractors.C: OTC does not refer to traffic control when discussing pilot fitness.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "PAVE" stand for as a risk assessment checklist?

options.text: PIC (or Pilot) – Aircraft – enVironment – External pressures.

explanation_correct: PAVE stands for Pilot, Aircraft, enVironment, External pressures — a structured checklist for assessing risk before and during flight.

explanation_distractors.B: PAVE does not include altitude or visibility. It evaluates four risk categories.
explanation_distractors.C: PAVE is not a process flow. It categorizes risk into Pilot, Aircraft, enVironment, and External pressures.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: POH stands for Pilot's Operating Handbook — the document containing operating procedures and performance data for a specific aircraft model.

explanation_distractors.B: POH is not a facility. It is the operating manual for the aircraft.
explanation_distractors.C: POH has nothing to do with hazards. It is the Pilot's Operating Handbook.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: SAO stands for Special Area of Operation — a designated area where certain operations or activities are conducted under specific conditions.

explanation_distractors.B: SAO is not an approach overlay. It designates special operational areas.
explanation_distractors.C: SAO does not refer to surveillance. It is a Special Area of Operation.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: SIGMET stands for Significant Meteorological Information — an advisory for weather significant to the safety of all aircraft, covering severe turbulence, severe icing, and widespread dust or sandstorms.

explanation_distractors.B: SIGMET is not an emergency transmission. It is a weather advisory product.
explanation_distractors.C: SIGMET has nothing to do with ground terminals. It is Significant Meteorological Information.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: SOP stands for Standard Operating Procedures — documented procedures to ensure consistency and safety in operations.

explanation_distractors.B: SOP does not specifically stand for Safety Operations Protocol, although SOPs improve safety.
explanation_distractors.C: SOP is not a scheduling plan. It is Standard Operating Procedures.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "TCU" stand for in weather reports?
explanation_correct: TCU stands for Towering Cumulus — rapidly growing cumulus clouds that may develop into cumulonimbus (thunderstorm) clouds. An indicator of atmospheric instability.

explanation_distractors.B: TCU in weather context is not a control unit. It identifies developing storm clouds.
explanation_distractors.C: TCU is not a turbulence update. It describes a specific cloud type.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: TFR stands for Temporary Flight Restriction — a temporary airspace restriction commonly issued for security, VIP movement, disasters, major events, or safety. TFRs are issued as FDC NOTAMs.

explanation_distractors.B: TFR is not related to frequencies. It restricts flight in a defined area temporarily.
explanation_distractors.C: TFR does not regulate traffic flow. It temporarily restricts flight in specific airspace.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "TN" stand for in navigation?
explanation_correct: TN stands for True North — the direction toward the geographic North Pole. It differs from magnetic north by the amount of magnetic variation.

explanation_distractors.B: TN is not about terminal navigation. It refers to the geographic North Pole direction.
explanation_distractors.C: TN does not mean Transition Notice. It stands for True North.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: TRSA stands for Terminal Radar Service Area — airspace surrounding certain airports where ATC provides radar services on a voluntary basis. Participation is not mandatory.

explanation_distractors.B: TRSA is not a restricted area. Participation in TRSA services is voluntary.
explanation_distractors.C: TRSA does not regulate routing. It is a voluntary radar service area.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: TUC stands for Time of Useful Consciousness — the time between losing pressurization (or oxygen supply) and the point where a person can no longer take effective action.

explanation_distractors.B: TUC is not a certificate. It measures the time available before incapacitation from hypoxia.
explanation_distractors.C: TUC has nothing to do with traffic. It is a physiological concept.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: UNICOM stands for Aeronautical Advisory Communications Stations — nongovernment facilities that may provide airport information at certain airports. Frequencies are shown on charts.

explanation_distractors.B: UNICOM is not a communications module. It is a nongovernment advisory facility.
explanation_distractors.C: UNICOM is not a navigation command. It provides airport advisory information.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time — the global time standard used in aviation. METARs, TAFs, and NOTAMs use UTC (also called Zulu time).

explanation_distractors.B: UTC is not about unmanned traffic. It is the universal time standard.
explanation_distractors.C: UTC has nothing to do with terminal communications. It is Coordinated Universal Time.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: VFR stands for Visual Flight Rules — the rules governing flight when there is sufficient visibility to navigate by visual reference. All Part 107 operations are conducted under VFR weather minimums.

explanation_distractors.B: VFR is not a frequency range. It is a set of flight rules for visual conditions.
explanation_distractors.C: VFR does not mean a verified route. It is Visual Flight Rules.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: On sectional charts, what does "VR" stand for?

options.text: Visual Routes (military training routes flown under VFR).

explanation_correct: VR stands for Visual Routes — military training routes flown under VFR. Like IR routes, routes with 4-digit numbers have segments at or below 1,500 ft AGL.

explanation_distractors.B: VR does not mean Variable Range. It identifies VFR military training routes.
explanation_distractors.C: VR is not a VFR restriction. It labels specific military training routes.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does "VO" stand for under Part 107?
explanation_correct: VO stands for Visual Observer — an optional crewmember who helps maintain situational awareness by watching the aircraft and scanning for hazards.

explanation_distractors.B: VO is not a verification officer. It is a crew role in sUAS operations.
explanation_distractors.C: VO does not refer to equipment output. It is the Visual Observer role.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: W&B stands for Weight and Balance — the process of verifying that an aircraft's weight is within limits and its center of gravity is within the allowable range.

explanation_distractors.B: W&B does not refer to weather instruments. It is about aircraft weight and its balance point.
explanation_distractors.C: W&B is not about navigation waypoints. It concerns Weight and Balance.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: WST stands for Convective Significant Meteorological Information — commonly called a Convective SIGMET, issued for severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, and significant convective activity.

explanation_distractors.B: WST is not a weather station. It is a convective weather advisory product.
explanation_distractors.C: WST does not refer to wind shear testing. It is a Convective SIGMET.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does the abbreviation "RPIC" stand for in Part 107 operations?
explanation_correct: RPIC stands for Remote Pilot in Command — the person who has final authority and responsibility for the operation and safety of a sUAS flight under Part 107.

explanation_distractors.B: There is no FAA term 'Registered Pilot Identification Code.' RPIC refers to Remote Pilot in Command.
explanation_distractors.C: RPIC does not stand for Instruction Certificate. It is the designated person in command of the flight.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: In FAA terminology, what does "sUAS" stand for?
explanation_correct: sUAS stands for Small Unmanned Aircraft System. Under Part 107, this generally means a drone weighing less than 55 pounds at takeoff, including everything on board or attached.

explanation_distractors.B: sUAS does not refer to surveillance. It describes the category of small unmanned aircraft systems under Part 107.
explanation_distractors.C: sUAS is not related to utility services. It is the regulatory term for small drones.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: METAR stands for Meteorological Aerodrome Report — a standardized current weather observation for an airport, usually issued hourly.

explanation_distractors.B: METAR is not an environmental analysis. It is a standardized airport weather observation.
explanation_distractors.C: METAR has nothing to do with elevation tracking. It reports current weather conditions.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: TAF stands for Terminal Aerodrome Forecast — a forecast of expected weather within 5 statute miles of the airport terminal area, usually covering 24 to 30 hours.

explanation_distractors.B: TAF is not a frequency. It is a weather forecast for the airport area.
explanation_distractors.C: TAF has nothing to do with terrain files. It forecasts airport weather conditions.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: VLOS stands for Visual Line of Sight — the requirement that the RPIC, the person manipulating the controls, or a VO must see the unmanned aircraft throughout the flight with unaided vision (except corrective lenses).

explanation_distractors.B: VLOS is not an operating standard level. It is a visual tracking requirement.
explanation_distractors.C: VLOS has nothing to do with launch systems. It requires visual contact with the drone.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: BVLOS stands for Beyond Visual Line of Sight — operating a drone when the crew cannot directly see it. This is not routine under Part 107 and generally requires a waiver.

explanation_distractors.B: BVLOS is not a location standard. It describes operating beyond the pilot's visual range.
explanation_distractors.C: BVLOS has nothing to do with landing. It means the drone is beyond unaided visual range.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: FRIA stands for FAA-Recognized Identification Area — a defined area where a drone without Remote ID equipment may operate if it stays within the FRIA and within VLOS.

explanation_distractors.B: FRIA has nothing to do with instrument approaches. It is a Remote ID exception area.
explanation_distractors.C: FRIA is not a flight restriction zone. It allows non-Remote-ID drones to fly in a defined area.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

options.text: Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability.
Local Airspace Advisory and Navigation Control.

explanation_correct: LAANC stands for Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability — the FAA system that automates many controlled-airspace authorization requests near airports through approved UAS Service Suppliers.

explanation_distractors.B: LAANC is not an advisory service. It automates airspace authorization for drone pilots.
explanation_distractors.C: LAANC is available for all Part 107 pilots, not just non-commercial operations.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

question_text: What does the "IMSAFE" checklist stand for?

options.text: Illness, Medication, Stress, Alcohol, Fatigue, Emotion.
Instrument, Maintenance, Safety, Aircraft, Fuel, Equipment.
Inspection, Mechanical, System, Alert, Frequency, Emergency.

explanation_correct: IMSAFE stands for Illness, Medication, Stress, Alcohol, Fatigue, Emotion — a personal readiness checklist pilots use to self-assess fitness for duty before flying.

explanation_distractors.B: IMSAFE is a personal fitness checklist, not an equipment inspection list.
explanation_distractors.C: IMSAFE has nothing to do with mechanical systems. It assesses pilot personal readiness.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3

explanation_correct: SRM stands for Single-Pilot Resource Management — using all available resources (automation, checklists, other people) when one pilot is solely responsible for the operation.

explanation_distractors.B: SRM is not about route mapping. It is about managing all available resources as a single pilot.
explanation_distractors.C: SRM is not a review manual. It is a pilot resource management concept.

source: FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide Appendix 3
